title: Palantir Changed The Number It Wants You To Judge It By
detail:
Palantir Changed The Number It Wants You To Judge It By
Trefis Team

PLTR
IBM
AMZN
GOOG
SNOW
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) used to report its total customer count on the quarterly earnings call. The latest call did not include it. In the count's place sits a bookings figure large enough to change what kind of business you are looking at, and the swap says more about what a holder owns than the headline growth rates do.

Palantir Used To Give A Company-Wide Customer Count On Its Earnings Calls

As recently as the first quarter of 2026 that count stood at 1,007. Counts were the pitch well before that: in the third quarter of 2024 management put U.S. commercial customers at 321, and a rising base was the proof that AIP, the company's AI platform, had found buyers outside the government work Palantir grew up on.

The second quarter of 2026 earnings call carries no company-wide count at all. The only one management still gives is the U.S. commercial figure, which counts a narrower population, at 653. There was no announcement that the company-wide count was being retired. The count simply stopped being a metric Palantir used to lead with.

Now Palantir Leads With The Value Of Contracts It Has Signed

What took its place is total contract value. In the second quarter of 2026, Palantir signed $2.132 billion of U.S. commercial bookings, up 153% year over year, and $5.964 billion over the past twelve months, against the company's $6.16 billion of revenue over the past twelve months. That value spreads across multi-year contracts, so it measures commitment ahead of revenue.

Set the count and the revenue beside each other, and the shape is plain. Over the past year the U.S. commercial customer count grew 35%. U.S. commercial revenue grew 149%. Revenue per customer is climbing far faster than the customer list, and net dollar retention across the company of 157% shows existing accounts expanding at the same time.

Management explains the expansion as customers climbing its own stack. Accounts that were only using Foundry now want Ontology and the whole sovereign AI stack, and that expansion lands in bookings long before it lands in revenue. Since the quarter closed, in early September 2026, Palantir widened its PwC alliance to push enterprise AI deeper inside big organizations.

What You Own Now Rides On How Big Each Account Gets

None of this reads as trouble. Revenue grew 93% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, the fastest Palantir has ever reported, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a midpoint of $8.154 billion, its largest full-year raise ever. If a rising outlook is what you are buying, our guidance-driven momentum screen tracks who is actually lifting one.

title: Does Quantum's Debt Elimination Strengthen Its Financial Position?
detail:
Does Quantum's Debt Elimination Strengthen Its Financial Position?
Vaishali Doshi
Wed, September 9, 2026 at 12:12 PM CDT 3 min read
IBM
NTAP
QMCO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Quantum Corporation QMCO strengthened its financial position after eliminating all outstanding debt in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. As of June 30, 2026, the company had no term debt or convertible notes outstanding compared with $54.8 million of term debt and $90 million of convertible notes on its balance sheet at the end of fiscal 2026.

The company eliminated the term debt through proceeds from a private placement. The company raised approximately $94.6 million in net proceeds by issuing roughly 10.6 million common shares. Quantum subsequently paid $57.8 million in aggregate for the termination of the Term Loan Credit Agreement. The sum included the outstanding principal amount, accrued interest and fees and expenses incurred in connection with the termination.

The convertible notes were converted into common shares and subsequently canceled, leaving the company without outstanding term-loan or convertible-note debt.

The debt elimination will reduce Quantum's interest expenses. Management noted that it expects interest expense to be "minimal" going forward following the debt elimination. It had $21.6 million of interest expense in fiscal 2026. For the fiscal first quarter, interest expense declined to $2.1 million from $6.5 million in the year-ago period.

Quantum Corporation Revenue (Quarterly)
Quantum Corporation Revenue (Quarterly)

Quantum Corporation revenue-quarterly | Quantum Corporation Quote

Quantum had $54.6 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash at the quarter-end. The company also delivered a cash flow from operating activities of $0.9 million compared with a $16.9 million outflow a year earlier. Quarterly revenues reached $80.8 million, up 25.7% year over year, driven by strong demand for ActiveScale and tape storage solutions.

With debt eliminated and improving operating performance, QMCO appears better positioned to fund growth initiatives and navigate ongoing supply constraints while pursuing sustainable profitability. However, the company needs to watch out for stiff competition from players such as International Business Machines IBM, EMC business unit of Dell and NetApp NTAP.

Mapping the Competitive Terrain

IBM and Quantum face off each other in the enterprise storage market, including object storage systems and tape storage systems. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that the company is gaining share in storage through its Flash, Fusion and tape offerings, including AI-powered capabilities that help clients scale and manage data for AI.

However,  the company's balance sheet has become more complex owing to its acquisition-led transformation. Total debt was $62 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026, while cash, restricted cash and marketable securities fell to $8.2 billion from $14.5 billion at 2025-end.

title: Circle Buys Payments Firm Tazapay For $400 Million
detail:
Circle Buys Payments Firm Tazapay For $400 Million
Editorial Staff

CRCL
USDC-USD
DX-Y.NYB
USDC
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (NYSE: $CRCL) has agreed to buy Singapore-based cross-border payments company Tazapay for $400 million U.S. in stock.

Circle, which issues the USDC stablecoin (CRYPTO: $USDC), said the final amount it pays for privately held Tazapay will depend on the payment firm's debt and transaction expenses.

Tazapay is a business-to-business payments firm that connects banks and financial technology companies, allowing them to collect and pay money in 100 markets worldwide.

According to its website, Tazapay processes more than $25 billion U.S. annually, with 60% of its transactions involving stablecoins.

Tazapay holds operating licenses in Singapore, Canada, Australia and the U.S., with applications underway in the European Union, Hong Kong and the United Arab Emirates.

Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies whose value is pegged to another asset, usually the U.S. dollar. They are ideal for moving money across blockchains globally.

Circle said in a news release that Tazapay will give it the last-mile infrastructure and network needed to move money globally via its USDC stablecoin.

Circle and Tazapay already have a relationship. Tazapay has helped design Circle Payments Network, according to the two companies.

In recent months, Circle has been on an acquisition spree. This July, it bought nearly 1,000 blockchain patents from technology giant IBM (NYSE: $IBM).

The Tazapay acquisition is expected to close in 2027, pending regulatory approvals.

CRCL stock has declined 19% over the last 12 months to trade at $96.18 U.S. per share.
